Naturality of the construction of F from phi_K shows that F(W_alpha^n)=W_alpha^n and F(V_{alpha,j}^n)=V_{alpha,j+1}^n, with indices modulo d_alpha. These restrictions are isomorphisms because phi_K is an isomorphism and it sends the j-th translate of L_{alpha,0} tensor M_alpha to the (j+1)-st translate. This is exactly the mapping property stated in the lemma. Note that we do not need L_{alpha,0} itself to carry an arithmetic Frobenius structure; only the composite F^{d_alpha} preserves V_{alpha,0}^n, and that is the operator considered below.

We now prove the purely linear algebra fact needed. Let C be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, let W = direct_sum_{j=0}^{d-1} U_j be finite-dimensional, and let T:W -> W be an invertible linear map with T(U_j)=U_{j+1} for all j modulo d. Put A = T^d|_{U_0}. Then T is semisimple on W if and only if A is semisimple on U_0.

First assume T is semisimple. Then T^d is semisimple, because a diagonalizable operator is diagonal in a basis of eigenvectors and taking the d-th power only raises the eigenvalues to d. The subspace U_0 is invariant under T^d since T^d(U_j)=U_j for every j. A restriction of a semisimple operator to an invariant subspace is semisimple: if S is semisimple with eigenspace decomposition W = direct_sum_mu E_mu, then an invariant subspace E is direct_sum_mu (E cap E_mu). Therefore A = T^d|_{U_0} is semisimple.

Conversely assume A is semisimple. Since T is invertible, A is invertible, so every eigenvalue of A is nonzero. Choose an eigenbasis v_1,...,v_r of U_0, with A v_s = lambda_s v_s. For each s and each d-th root eta of lambda_s in C, define w_{s,eta} = sum_{j=0}^{d-1} eta^{-j} T^j v_s. Then T w_{s,eta} = eta w_{s,eta}, because T^d v_s = A v_s = lambda_s v_s = eta^d v_s. We claim that the vectors w_{s,eta} form a basis of W. For fixed s, the d vectors w_{s,eta} are independent: a relation sum_eta a_eta w_{s,eta}=0, after comparing coefficients of T^j v_s for j=0,...,d-1, gives sum_eta a_eta eta^{-j}=0. The matrix (eta^{-j})_{j,eta} is a Vandermonde matrix with distinct nonzero columns, hence invertible in characteristic 0, so all a_eta=0. The same invertible Vandermonde change of basis shows span{w_{s,eta}} = span{T^j v_s: 0 <= j <= d-1}, and this span has dimension d.

It remains to check that the family {T^j v_s}_{s,j} is a basis of W. It spans W because T^j:U_0 -> U_j is an isomorphism, so every element of U_j is T^j u for some u in U_0, and u is a linear combination of the v_s. For independence, suppose sum_{s,j} c_{s,j} T^j v_s = 0. Let pi_0:W -> U_0 be the projection along the direct-sum decomposition. Apply pi_0 T^k for k=0,...,d-1. If k=0, the U_0 component is sum_s c_{s,0} v_s. If k>0, the only terms contributing to U_0 are those with j+k=d, and their contribution is sum_s c_{s,d-k} T^d v_s = sum_s c_{s,d-k} lambda_s v_s. Since the v_s are independent and lambda_s is nonzero, all c_{s,j} vanish. Thus {T^j v_s} is a basis, and the blockwise Vandermonde transformation from this basis to {w_{s,eta}} is invertible. Hence T has an eigenbasis and is semisimple. This proves the linear algebra fact.

Apply the fact to each orbit alpha. For fixed alpha, take W = W_alpha^n, U_j = V_{alpha,j}^n, T = F|_{W_alpha^n}, and d = d_alpha. The hypotheses are satisfied, and the operator A is exactly F^{d_alpha}|_{V_{alpha,0}^n} = F_alpha^{d_alpha}. Therefore F is semisimple on W_alpha^n if and only if F_alpha^{d_alpha} is semisimple on V_{alpha,0}^n.

Finally, V^n = direct_sum_alpha W_alpha^n and each W_alpha^n is F-stable. A block diagonal operator on a finite direct sum is semisimple if and only if each block is semisimple: if each block has an eigenbasis, their union is an eigenbasis of the whole space; conversely, if the whole operator is semisimple, each invariant summand inherits a semisimple restriction. Combining this with the previous paragraph gives that F is semisimple on V^n if and only if, for every alpha, F_alpha^{d_alpha} is semisimple on V_{alpha,0}^n.

This completes the proof. We did not use the purity hypothesis to deduce semisimplicity; purity is irrelevant to this reduction. The multiplicity space M_alpha is kept inside V_{alpha,0}^n, so the operator F_alpha^{d_alpha} includes any nontrivial action of F^{d_alpha} on M_alpha. The proof also avoids requiring an arithmetic Frobenius structure on a single constituent L_{alpha,0} when its orbit has length d_alpha.

lemma_20a.statement: Let V and W be bounded complexes of finite-dimensional Q_l-vector spaces, and let T_V:V→V and T_W:W→W be automorphisms in the derived category. Suppose that for every integer n, H^n(V), with the automorphism induced by T_V, is pure of weight w+n, and H^n(W), with the automorphism induced by T_W, is pure of weight v+n; that is, all eigenvalues of the induced automorphisms have the stated weights. Then for every integer m, H^m(RHom(V,W)), with the induced automorphism f ↦ T_W ∘ f ∘ T_V^{-1}, is pure of weight v-w+m. More explicitly, there is a (T_W,T_V)-equivariant isomorphism of graded vector spaces H^m(RHom(V,W)) ≅ ⊕_n Hom(H^n(V), H^{n+m}(W)), and on the summand indexed by n the eigenvalues are ratios β/α, where α is an eigenvalue of T_V on H^n(V) and β is an eigenvalue of T_W on H^{n+m}(W), hence have weight (v+n+m)-(w+n)=v-w+m. Equivalently, RHom(V,W) is pure of weight v-w. Moreover, if every H^n(V) is semisimple as a T_V-module and every H^n(W) is semisimple as a T_W-module, then each H^m(RHom(V,W)) is semisimple as a module under the induced automorphism.
lemma_20a.proof:
Proof. Work in the derived category D^b(Vec_{Q_l}). Put A_n = H^n(V), B_k = H^k(W). Let S_n : A_n -> A_n and R_k : B_k -> B_k be the automorphisms induced by T_V and T_W. Since T_V and T_W are automorphisms in the derived category, S_n and R_k are invertible.

1. Formal splitting. Because Q_l is a field, every bounded complex of finite-dimensional Q_l-vector spaces is isomorphic in D^b(Vec_{Q_l}) to the direct sum of its cohomology groups shifted to their degrees. Explicitly, choose for each n a decomposition V^n = H^n + E^n + C^n such that H^n maps isomorphically to the cohomology H^n(V), E^n is the boundary subspace, and d(C^n)=E^{n+1} with d|C^n: C^n -> E^{n+1} an isomorphism. This gives a chain decomposition of V into (direct sum_n H^n[-n]) plus a contractible complex. The two-term summands C^n -> E^{n+1} are contractible because the inverse isomorphism E^{n+1} -> C^n gives a contracting homotopy. Hence the projection to H_V := direct sum_n A_n[-n] is a quasi-isomorphism inducing the identity on cohomology. Choose such quasi-isomorphisms alpha_V: V -> H_V and alpha_W: W -> H_W := direct sum_k B_k[-k].

Conjugate the automorphisms: T'_V = alpha_V T_V alpha_V^{-1} on H_V and T'_W = alpha_W T_W alpha_W^{-1} on H_W. For n != k, Hom_D(A_n[-n], A_k[-k]) = 0, because A_n and A_k are vector spaces concentrated in degree 0 and Ext^r(A_n,A_k)=0 for r != 0 over a field. Thus every endomorphism of H_V is block diagonal. Since T'_V induces S_n on H^n, we have T'_V = direct sum_n S_n. Similarly T'_W = direct sum_k R_k.

The map beta: RHom(V,W) -> RHom(H_V,H_W), f -> alpha_W f alpha_V^{-1}, is an isomorphism in the derived category. It is equivariant for the induced automorphisms: beta(T_W f T_V^{-1}) = T'_W beta(f) T'_V^{-1}. Therefore it gives, for each m, a (T_W,T_V)-equivariant isomorphism of Q_l-vector spaces H^m(RHom(V,W)) isomorphic to H^m(RHom(H_V,H_W)).

2. Identification of the graded pieces. We compute
H^m(RHom(H_V,H_W)) = Hom_D(H_V, H_W[m])
isomorphic to direct sum_{n,k} Hom_D(A_n[-n], B_k[-k][m]).
For vector spaces A_n and B_k concentrated in degree 0, Hom_D(A_n, B_k[r]) is Hom(A_n,B_k) if r=0 and is 0 otherwise. Hence the (n,k)-summand is nonzero exactly when m = k-n, i.e. k = n+m, and then it is Hom(A_n,B_{n+m}). Thus there is a (T_W,T_V)-equivariant isomorphism
H^m(RHom(V,W)) isomorphic to direct sum_n Hom(A_n, B_{n+m}),
where the sum is finite because V and W are bounded, and the induced automorphism on the n-th summand is
U_{n,m}: Hom(A_n,B_{n+m}) -> Hom(A_n,B_{n+m}), f -> R_{n+m} f S_n^{-1}.
This proves the explicit decomposition in the statement. If there are no indices n with both A_n and B_{n+m} nonzero, the space is 0 and all claims are vacuous.

3. Spectrum of one summand. Fix n and put k=n+m. Extend scalars to K = Q_l_bar. Write A = A_n tensor K, B = B_k tensor K, S = S_n tensor K, R = R_k tensor K. Identify Hom_K(A,B) with B tensor A^*. Under this identification, U_{n,m} tensor K is R tensor (S^{-1})^*.

We choose triangular bases independently, avoiding any dual-basis issue. Since K is algebraically closed, the endomorphism R of B has a complete invariant flag; choose a basis b_1,...,b_r of B in which R is upper triangular, with diagonal entries beta_1,...,beta_r. The diagonal entries of an upper triangular matrix are its eigenvalues with algebraic multiplicity, so the beta_j are the eigenvalues of R. Likewise, (S^{-1})^* is an endomorphism of the vector space A^*, so choose a basis a_1^*,...,a_s^* of A^* in which (S^{-1})^* is upper triangular, with diagonal entries gamma_1,...,gamma_s. If alpha_1,...,alpha_s are the eigenvalues of S, then gamma_i = alpha_i^{-1}: S and S^* have the same characteristic polynomial, and inverting S replaces each eigenvalue alpha by alpha^{-1}.

Order the tensor basis b_j tensor a_i^* lexicographically. If R b_j = sum_{p<=j} c_{pj} b_p and (S^{-1})^* a_i^* = sum_{q<=i} d_{qi} a_q^*, then
(R tensor (S^{-1})^*)(b_j tensor a_i^*) = sum_{p<=j, q<=i} c_{pj} d_{qi} b_p tensor a_q^*.
Thus the matrix of R tensor (S^{-1})^* in this basis is upper triangular, and its diagonal entries are c_{jj} d_{ii} = beta_j alpha_i^{-1}. Therefore the eigenvalues of U_{n,m} on Hom_K(A_n tensor K, B_k tensor K) are exactly the ratios beta/alpha, where beta runs over eigenvalues of R_k and alpha over eigenvalues of S_n, with the expected multiplicities.

4. Purity. By hypothesis, every eigenvalue alpha of S_n has Weil absolute value q^{(w+n)/2}, and every eigenvalue beta of R_k has Weil absolute value q^{(v+k)/2}. For k=n+m,
|beta alpha^{-1}| = q^{(v+k)/2} q^{-(w+n)/2} = q^{(v-w+m)/2}.
Thus each summand Hom(A_n,B_{n+m}) is pure of weight v-w+m. The eigenvalues of a finite direct sum are the union of the eigenvalues of the summands, so the finite direct sum is again pure of that weight. Hence H^m(RHom(V,W)) is pure of weight v-w+m. This is equivalent to saying that RHom(V,W) is pure of weight v-w.

5. Semisimplicity. Assume now that each A_n is semisimple as a module under S_n and each B_k is semisimple as a module under R_k. After extending scalars to K, S_n and R_k are diagonalizable. Therefore R_k is diagonalizable, S_n^{-1} is diagonalizable, and (S_n^{-1})^* is diagonalizable. Choose eigenbases of B_k for R_k and of A_n^* for (S_n^{-1})^*. In the tensor-product eigenbasis of Hom_K(A_n tensor K, B_k tensor K), the operator U_{n,m} is diagonal, with eigenvalues beta_j alpha_i^{-1}. Hence U_{n,m} is diagonalizable over K, and by lemma_5 it is semisimple over Q_l.

For fixed m, the operator on H^m(RHom(V,W)) is, under the equivariant isomorphism of Step 2, the finite direct sum of the operators U_{n,m} on Hom(A_n,B_{n+m}). By lemma_9 this direct sum is semisimple. Since the isomorphism in Step 2 is Q_l-linear and conjugates the operators, lemma_8 transfers semisimplicity to H^m(RHom(V,W)) with its induced automorphism. This completes the proof.

lemma_14.statement: Let X be a smooth projective variety over F_q of pure dimension d. In D^b_c(X_{Fbar_q}, Q_l), there is a canonical arithmetic-Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism RHom(Q_l[d], Q_l[d]) = Q_l, where Q_l[d] is the shifted constant sheaf and Q_l on the right is the constant sheaf.
lemma_14.proof: Proof. Let k = overline{F}_q and Xbar = X_k. Write sigma(a)=a^q and F_ar=(id_X x sigma)^* for arithmetic Frobenius. Here RHom denotes the derived internal Hom object in D^b_c(Xbar,Q_l). Denote by Q_l the constant sheaf on Xbar and set L=Q_l[d]. If X is empty, both sides are the zero object, so assume X is nonempty. The constant sheaf has a canonical arithmetic Frobenius structure alpha: F_ar^* Q_l -> Q_l, namely the identity under the canonical identification F_ar^* Q_l = Q_l. Hence L has the induced structure alpha_L=alpha[d]: F_ar^* L=(F_ar^* Q_l)[d] -> Q_l[d]=L. In D^b_c(Xbar,Q_l), L is tensor-invertible, with inverse L^{-1}=Q_l[-d]. Let ev: L^{-1} tensor L -> Q_l be the canonical evaluation isomorphism, i.e. the standard shift and unit isomorphism. For every object B, after the usual associativity and commutativity isomorphisms, the adjoint of ev tensor id_B gives a canonical natural isomorphism theta_B: L^{-1} tensor B -> RHom(L,B). For B=L, define psi: RHom(L,L) -> Q_l by psi=ev o theta_L^{-1}. Equivalently, psi^{-1}: Q_l -> RHom(L,L) is the canonical map sending the unit 1 to id_L; this fixes the orientation of the desired isomorphism. Now equip RHom(L,L) with its induced arithmetic Frobenius structure. Internal Hom is contravariant in the first variable and covariant in the second. The canonical comparison for pullback gives an isomorphism F_ar^* RHom(L,L) -> RHom(F_ar^* L, F_ar^* L). Composing with RHom(alpha_L^{-1}, alpha_L) gives Phi_RHom: F_ar^* RHom(L,L) -> RHom(L,L). On morphisms this is conjugation u -> alpha_L o u o alpha_L^{-1}. Equip L^{-1} with the inverse arithmetic Frobenius structure beta: F_ar^* L^{-1} -> L^{-1}. Concretely, using the canonical identification L^{-1}=RHom(L,Q_l), take beta=RHom(alpha_L^{-1}, alpha). Equivalently, beta is the unique structure making ev equivariant, namely ev o (beta tensor alpha_L)=alpha o F_ar^* ev. The structure on L^{-1} tensor L is beta tensor alpha_L. In the present case alpha is the identity, so alpha_L and beta are identities and beta tensor alpha_L is the identity on Q_l. The isomorphism theta_B is natural with respect to tensor products and internal Hom and compatible with the comparison isomorphisms for F_ar^*. Therefore theta_L is Frobenius-equivariant: theta_L o (beta tensor alpha_L)=Phi_RHom o F_ar^* theta_L. Taking inverses gives theta_L^{-1} o Phi_RHom=(beta tensor alpha_L) o F_ar^* theta_L^{-1}. Composing with ev and using the equivariance of ev yields psi o Phi_RHom=alpha o F_ar^* psi. In diagrammatic form, the square with horizontal arrows Phi_RHom and alpha and vertical arrows F_ar^* psi and psi commutes. This is exactly the arithmetic-Frobenius-equivariance of psi. Since psi is a canonical isomorphism and satisfies the equivariance relation, we obtain a canonical arithmetic-Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism RHom(Q_l[d],Q_l[d])=Q_l. QED.

lemma_27.statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let X be a smooth projective variety over F_q, and let l != p be a prime. Write Xbar for X base changed to an algebraic closure of F_q, and let C_1,...,C_m be the geometric connected components of Xbar. For every integer n>=0, the restrictions to the components give a canonical decomposition H^n_et(Xbar,Q_l) = direct sum_{j=1}^m H^n_et(C_j,Q_l), and arithmetic Frobenius F_q permutes the summands according to its action on the set {C_1,...,C_m}. Let O_1,...,O_r be the orbits of this action, choose one component C_s in each orbit O_s, and let m_s be the length of O_s. Then arithmetic Frobenius F_q acts semisimply on H^n_et(Xbar,Q_l) if and only if, for every s=1,...,r, the operator F_q^{m_s} acts semisimply on H^n_et(C_s,Q_l). Equivalently, F_q^{m_s} is the arithmetic Frobenius over F_{q^{m_s}} on the F_{q^{m_s}}-model of the geometrically connected component C_s. In particular, the Frobenius-semisimplicity conjecture for smooth projective varieties reduces to the case of geometrically connected smooth projective varieties over finite fields.
lemma_27.proof:
Proof. Put k = Fbar_q and let sigma: k -> k be sigma(a)=a^q. Let tau = id_X x sigma be the arithmetic Frobenius morphism on Xbar = X_k. By lemma_6a, the pullback tau^* is a Q_l-linear automorphism of H^n_et(Xbar,Q_l); denote it by F_q.

1. Decomposition by geometric components. The scheme Xbar is the finite disjoint union of its geometric connected components C_1,...,C_m, each open and closed. For a finite disjoint union, restriction gives a canonical isomorphism H^n_et(Xbar,Q_l) -> direct sum_j H^n_et(C_j,Q_l). Indeed, if i_j:C_j -> Xbar are the inclusions, the constant sheaf Q_l on Xbar is the direct sum of i_{j*}Q_l, and taking derived global sections gives a direct sum decomposition.

Let V_j = H^n_et(C_j,Q_l). Since tau is an automorphism of Xbar, it permutes the components C_j. Because cohomology is contravariant, if tau(C_j)=C_k, then F_q = tau^* maps V_k isomorphically onto V_j; equivalently F_q(V_j)=V_{tau^{-1}(j)}. Thus the induced permutation of the summands has the same orbits and the same orbit lengths as the permutation of the components.

2. Orbit decomposition. Let O_1,...,O_r be the orbits of tau on {C_1,...,C_m}. Choose C_s in O_s and let m_s = |O_s|. Index the components in O_s by C_{s,j} = tau^{-j}(C_s) for j modulo m_s. Then tau(C_{s,j})=C_{s,j-1}, and hence F_q(V_{s,j})=V_{s,j+1}, where V_{s,j}=H^n_et(C_{s,j},Q_l). Put W_s = direct sum_{j=0}^{m_s-1} V_{s,j}. Then H^n_et(Xbar,Q_l) = direct sum_{s=1}^r W_s, and F_q(W_s)=W_s.

3. Field of definition of a chosen component. By construction tau^{m_s}(C_s)=C_s, and m_s is minimal with this property. The stabilizer of C_s in the topologically cyclic group Gal(k/F_q) is therefore the closed subgroup generated by sigma^{m_s}; its fixed field is F_{q^{m_s}}. Hence C_s is stable under Gal(k/F_{q^{m_s}}). Equivalently, C_s is cut out by a global idempotent e_s in the structure sheaf of Xbar, and Galois stability means that e_s is fixed by Gal(k/F_{q^{m_s}}). Idempotents descend along the faithfully flat morphism Spec k -> Spec F_{q^{m_s}}, so e_s descends to an idempotent on X_{F_{q^{m_s}}}, defining a unique open and closed subscheme C_s^{(m_s)} of X_{F_{q^{m_s}}} whose base change to k is C_s. This descended component is smooth projective and geometrically connected. The morphism tau^{m_s} on C_s is exactly the arithmetic Frobenius morphism over F_{q^{m_s}}, namely id x sigma^{m_s}. Therefore the induced operator F_q^{m_s} on H^n_et(C_s,Q_l) is the arithmetic Frobenius operator for the F_{q^{m_s}}-model C_s^{(m_s)}.

4. Finite-dimensionality. For each s, apply lemma_3 to the smooth projective variety C_s^{(m_s)} over F_{q^{m_s}}. It identifies H^n_et(C_s,Q_l) with Ext^n_{D^b_c(C_s,Q_l)}(IC,IC), where IC is the base change of IC_{C_s^{(m_s)}} to C_s. By lemma_17 this Ext group is finite-dimensional over Q_l. Since F_q^j: V_{s,0} -> V_{s,j} is an isomorphism, every V_{s,j} and every W_s is finite-dimensional.

5. Semisimplicity criterion. By lemma_9, F_q is semisimple on direct sum_s W_s if and only if F_q|W_s is semisimple for every s. Fix s. The restriction T_s = F_q|W_s is an automorphism of W_s = direct sum_{j=0}^{m_s-1} V_{s,j} with T_s(V_{s,j}) = V_{s,j+1} modulo m_s. Lemma_25 applies and says that T_s is semisimple on W_s if and only if T_s^{m_s} restricted to V_{s,0} is semisimple on V_{s,0}. But T_s^{m_s}|V_{s,0} = F_q^{m_s}|H^n_et(C_s,Q_l). Hence F_q is semisimple on H^n_et(Xbar,Q_l) if and only if for every s, F_q^{m_s} is semisimple on H^n_et(C_s,Q_l). The choice of representative in the orbit is immaterial, because relabeling the cyclic indexing gives the same criterion. This proves the stated equivalence, together with the interpretation of F_q^{m_s} from step 3.

6. Reduction of the conjecture. The conjecture is stated for geometric Frobenius. By lemma_6a, geometric Frobenius is the inverse of arithmetic Frobenius. By lemma_4, an invertible operator is semisimple if and only if its inverse is semisimple. By lemma_5, semisimplicity over Q_l is equivalent to diagonalizability after tensoring with Q_l_bar. Thus it is equivalent to prove arithmetic semisimplicity.

For an arbitrary smooth projective X over F_q, step 5 reduces arithmetic semisimplicity of F_q on H^n_et(Xbar,Q_l) to arithmetic semisimplicity of F_{q^{m_s}} on H^n_et(C_s,Q_l) for the geometrically connected smooth projective varieties C_s^{(m_s)} over the finite fields F_{q^{m_s}}. Therefore, if the conjecture is known for all geometrically connected smooth projective varieties over all finite fields, it follows for every smooth projective variety. The converse is the special case m=1. This completes the proof.

lemma_31.statement: Let X be a smooth projective variety over F_q, let ell != p, and let F be the q-power arithmetic Frobenius automorphism acting on the geometrically connected components of X_{Fbar_q}. For each geometrically connected component C, let d_C be the size of its F-orbit, so that F^{d_C} preserves C and induces a finite-dimensional Q_ell-linear automorphism on H^n_et(C,Q_ell) for every n. If F^{d_C} is semisimple on H^n_et(C,Q_ell) for every geometrically connected component C and every n, then F is semisimple on H^n_et(X_{Fbar_q},Q_ell) for every n.
lemma_31.proof: Fix n >= 0. Write Xbar = X_{Fbar_q} and V = H^n_et(Xbar,Q_l). Let {C} be the set of geometrically connected components of Xbar and put V_C = H^n_et(C,Q_l). Lemma_27 gives a canonical direct-sum decomposition V = direct sum_C V_C, and says that the q-power arithmetic Frobenius F permutes the summands according to its action on the components. The hypothesis states that each V_C is finite-dimensional; since there are only finitely many components, V is finite-dimensional. By lemma_6a, F is a Q_l-linear automorphism of V. If there are no components, then V=0 and semisimplicity is vacuous. Assume otherwise. For each component C, let F(C) be the component whose summand is the image of V_C under F. Then F(V_C)=V_{F(C)}, and because F is an automorphism of V, the restriction F|_{V_C}: V_C -> V_{F(C)} is an isomorphism. Let O run over the F-orbits on the set of components. Choose C_0 in O and let d = |O| = d_{C_0}. Enumerate O as C_j = F^j(C_0) for j=0,...,d-1, with C_d=C_0. Set W_O = direct sum_{j=0}^{d-1} V_{C_j}. Then V = direct sum_O W_O and each W_O is F-stable. Let T_O = F|_{W_O}. For every j modulo d, T_O(V_{C_j}) = V_{C_{j+1}}, with indices taken modulo d. By lemma_25, applied to the finite-dimensional spaces V_{C_0},...,V_{C_{d-1}} and the automorphism T_O of W_O, T_O is semisimple on W_O if and only if T_O^d restricted to V_{C_0} is semisimple on V_{C_0}. But T_O^d|_{V_{C_0}} = F^d|_{V_{C_0}} = F^{d_{C_0}} acting on H^n_et(C_0,Q_l). The hypothesis gives that this operator is semisimple. Hence T_O is semisimple on W_O. This holds for every orbit O. Finally, lemma_9 says that the direct-sum operator direct sum_O T_O on direct sum_O W_O is semisimple if and only if each T_O is semisimple. Since F on V is exactly direct sum_O T_O, F is semisimple on V. As n was arbitrary, F is semisimple on H^n_et(Xbar,Q_l) for every n.

lemma_35.statement: Let V and W be finite-dimensional \mathbb Q_\ell-vector spaces and let T:V\to V and S:W\to W be invertible linear operators. (i) If T is semisimple on V and S is semisimple on W, then T\otimes S is semisimple on V\otimes_{\mathbb Q_\ell}W. (ii) If U\subset V is a T-stable direct summand and T is semisimple on V, then T|_U is semisimple on U. (iii) If m\ge 1 and T^m is semisimple on V, then T is semisimple on V.
lemma_35.proof:
Proof. Let K = Q_l_bar. We first record two elementary facts. By lemma_5, for any finite-dimensional Q_l-vector space X and any linear operator A on X, A is semisimple over Q_l if and only if A_K = A tensor id_K is diagonalizable over K. Second, over the algebraically closed field K, a linear operator A on a finite-dimensional K-vector space E is diagonalizable if and only if its minimal polynomial m_A(x) is square-free. For the forward implication, if A is diagonalizable with distinct eigenvalues lambda_1,...,lambda_r, then product_{s=1}^r (A - lambda_s I) = 0, so m_A divides product_{s=1}^r (x - lambda_s), a square-free polynomial. For the reverse implication, if m_A(x)=product_{s=1}^r (x-lambda_s) with distinct lambda_s, then the ideals (x-lambda_s) are pairwise comaximal. The Chinese remainder theorem gives polynomials e_s(x) such that e_s(x) is congruent to 1 modulo (x-lambda_s) and to 0 modulo (x-lambda_t) for t not equal s. Then e_s(A) are commuting idempotents, sum_s e_s(A)=id_E, and im(e_s(A))=ker(A-lambda_s I). Hence E is a direct sum of eigenspaces, so A is diagonalizable.

Now prove the three assertions. If a vector space is zero-dimensional, the assertion is immediate, so assume dimensions are positive when choosing eigenbases.

(i) Suppose T and S are semisimple. By lemma_5, T_K and S_K are diagonalizable. Choose eigenbases {v_a} of V_K and {w_b} of W_K, with T_K v_a = alpha_a v_a and S_K w_b = beta_b w_b. The tensors {v_a tensor w_b} form a basis of V_K tensor_K W_K, which is canonically (V tensor_{Q_l} W)_K. Moreover (T tensor S)_K = T_K tensor S_K. Therefore (T tensor S)_K(v_a tensor w_b) = (T_K v_a) tensor (S_K w_b) = alpha_a beta_b (v_a tensor w_b). Thus every basis vector is an eigenvector, so T_K tensor S_K is diagonalizable. By lemma_5, T tensor S is semisimple on V tensor_{Q_l} W.

(ii) Suppose U subset V is a T-stable direct summand and T is semisimple. Choose U' with V = U directsum U'. Tensoring with K gives V_K = U_K directsum U'_K, and T_K(U_K) subset U_K. By lemma_5, T_K is diagonalizable on V_K. By the criterion, m_{T_K}(x) is square-free. Since m_{T_K}(T_K)=0 on V_K, its restriction also annihilates U_K, so m_{T_K|U_K} divides m_{T_K}. A divisor of a square-free polynomial is square-free. Hence m_{T_K|U_K} is square-free, and the criterion gives that T_K|U_K is diagonalizable. By lemma_5 again, T|U is semisimple on U.

(iii) Suppose m>=1 and T^m is semisimple. Let A = T_K. By lemma_5, A^m = (T^m)_K is diagonalizable. Since T is invertible, A is invertible, hence A^m is invertible. If V_K=0, then A is trivially diagonalizable. Otherwise, let m_{A^m}(y) be the minimal polynomial of A^m. By the criterion and invertibility, m_{A^m}(y)=product_{beta in B}(y-beta), where B is a finite set of distinct nonzero elements of K. Consider p(x)=m_{A^m}(x^m)=product_{beta in B}(x^m-beta). Then p(A)=m_{A^m}(A^m)=0, so m_A(x) divides p(x). We claim p is square-free. Let alpha in K be a root of p. Then alpha^m=beta for a unique beta in B. Since beta is nonzero, alpha is nonzero. The derivative is p'(x)=sum_{gamma in B} m x^{m-1} product_{delta in B, delta not equal gamma}(x^m-delta). At x=alpha, all summands with gamma not equal beta vanish because they contain the factor alpha^m-beta=0, while the summand with gamma=beta equals m alpha^{m-1} product_{delta in B, delta not equal beta}(beta-delta), which is nonzero since char(K)=0, alpha is nonzero, and the elements of B are distinct. Thus p'(alpha) is nonzero for every root alpha of p, so p has no repeated roots; over K this means p is square-free. Therefore m_A divides a square-free polynomial, so m_A is square-free. By the criterion, A is diagonalizable. Finally, lemma_5 implies T is semisimple on V.

This completes the proof.

lemma_36.statement: Let f:Y\to X be a finite surjective morphism of smooth projective geometrically connected varieties over \mathbb F_q, of degree d. For every i\ge 0, the pullback f^*:H^i_{\mathrm{et}}(X_{\overline{\mathbb F}_q},\mathbb Q_\ell)\to H^i_{\mathrm{et}}(Y_{\overline{\mathbb F}_q},\mathbb Q_\ell) is injective and equivariant for arithmetic Frobenius, and the trace map f_*:H^i_{\mathrm{et}}(Y_{\overline{\mathbb F}_q},\mathbb Q_\ell)\to H^i_{\mathrm{et}}(X_{\overline{\mathbb F}_q},\mathbb Q_\ell) satisfies f_*\circ f^*=d\,\operatorname{id}. Consequently H^i_{\mathrm{et}}(X_{\overline{\mathbb F}_q},\mathbb Q_\ell) is a Frobenius-equivariant direct summand of H^i_{\mathrm{et}}(Y_{\overline{\mathbb F}_q},\mathbb Q_\ell), with retraction (1/d)f_*.
lemma_36.proof:
Let k be an algebraic closure of F_q. For Z = X or Y write H^i(Z) = H^i_et(Z_k,Q_l), and write F_Z for the arithmetic Frobenius automorphism of H^i(Z). All maps below are Q_l-linear.

1. Finite flatness and degree. Since X and Y are smooth projective and geometrically connected over F_q, X_k and Y_k are smooth, projective, connected, hence irreducible. The finite surjective morphism f_k:Y_k -> X_k preserves dimension; set n = dim X_k = dim Y_k. For y in Y_k and x=f(y), the local ring A=O_{X_k,x} is regular local, B=O_{Y_k,y} is regular local and therefore Cohen-Macaulay, and B is a finite A-module. By the local miracle-flatness criterion, B is flat over A. Hence f_k is finite locally free. Because X_k is connected, the rank of f_{k,*}O_{Y_k} is constant; this rank is the degree d = [k(Y_k):k(X_k)]. In particular every geometric fiber has scheme-theoretic length d. No separability hypothesis is used.

2. Poincare duality and the trace map. For a smooth projective n-dimensional variety Z over k, Poincare duality gives perfect cup-product pairings
   H^i(Z) x H^{2n-i}(Z) -> Q_l(-n),
where Q_l(-n) is the Tate twist on which arithmetic Frobenius acts by multiplication by q^n. The trace isomorphism tr_Z:H^{2n}(Z)->Q_l(-n) sends the cycle class of a zero-cycle of degree m to m. These pairings are functorial for morphisms and Frobenius-equivariant.

First we record the top-degree formula
   tr_Y o f^* = d tr_X.
Choose a closed point x in X_k. Since f_k is finite locally free of rank d, flat pullback of the zero-cycle [x] is the scheme-theoretic fiber Y_x, a zero-dimensional k-scheme of length d, hence of degree d. Functoriality of cycle classes gives f^* cl_X([x]) = cl_Y([Y_x]). Applying tr_Y and tr_X and using that H^{2n}(Z) is one-dimensional for connected Z gives the formula.

Define f_*:H^i(Y)->H^i(X) as the adjoint of f^* with respect to the Poincare pairings: for alpha in H^{2n-i}(X) and beta in H^i(Y),
   <alpha, f_* beta>_X = <f^* alpha, beta>_Y.
Perfectness of the pairing gives a unique f_* beta. This is the cohomological trace map for the finite morphism f.

3. The composition formula. If i is outside 0 <= i <= 2n, both H^i(X) and H^i(Y) vanish by Poincare duality, so the assertions are trivial. Assume 0 <= i <= 2n. For alpha in H^i(X) and gamma in H^{2n-i}(X),
   <gamma, f_* f^* alpha>_X
     = <f^* gamma, f^* alpha>_Y
     = tr_Y(f^* gamma cup f^* alpha)
     = tr_Y(f^*(gamma cup alpha))
     = d tr_X(gamma cup alpha)
     = d <gamma, alpha>_X.
Since the pairing is perfect, f_* f^* alpha = d alpha. Hence f_* o f^* = d id.

4. Injectivity and direct summand. The integer d is nonzero, hence invertible in Q_l. If f^* alpha = 0, then d alpha = f_* f^* alpha = 0, so alpha = 0. Thus f^* is injective. The map s = (1/d) f_* satisfies s o f^* = id, so H^i(X) identifies with im f^* and is a direct summand of H^i(Y), with complement ker s.

5. Equivariance for arithmetic Frobenius. Let sigma:k->k be sigma(a)=a^q. By lemma_6a, F_Z = (id_Z x sigma)^* on cohomology. Since f is defined over F_q, the square
   Y_k --f_k--> X_k
    |F_Y          |F_X
   Y_k --f_k--> X_k
commutes. Functoriality of pullback gives f^* o F_X = F_Y o f^*.

For f_*, use the adjoint definition and Frobenius-equivariance of the pairings. For beta in H^i(Y) and alpha in H^{2n-i}(X),
   <F_X alpha, F_X(f_* beta)>_X
     = F_{Q_l(-n)} <alpha, f_* beta>_X
     = F_{Q_l(-n)} <f^* alpha, beta>_Y
     = <F_Y f^* alpha, F_Y beta>_Y
     = <f^* F_X alpha, F_Y beta>_Y
     = <F_X alpha, f_* F_Y beta>_X.
Perfectness implies F_X f_* beta = f_* F_Y beta. Thus f_* is Frobenius-equivariant, and so is s=(1/d)f_*. Therefore im f^* and ker s are stable under arithmetic Frobenius, and H^i_et(X_{bar F_q},Q_l) is a Frobenius-equivariant direct summand of H^i_et(Y_{bar F_q},Q_l).

lemma_39.statement: Let Y be a proper variety over \mathbb{F}_q, let \ell\neq p, let k=\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q, and write X=Y_k. Let F_Y:X\to X be the q-power arithmetic Frobenius automorphism. Let K,L\in D^b_c(X,\mathbb{Q}_\ell) be equipped with arithmetic Frobenius isomorphisms \varphi_K:F_Y^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}K and \varphi_L:F_Y^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}L. Let c_{K,L}:F_Y^*R\mathcal{H}om_X(K,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal{H}om_X(F_Y^*K,F_Y^*L) be the canonical comparison isomorphism, and define the induced arithmetic Frobenius isomorphism \varphi_{\mathcal{H}om}:F_Y^*R\mathcal{H}om_X(K,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal{H}om_X(K,L) to be the composite R\mathcal{H}om(\varphi_K^{-1},\varphi_L)\circ c_{K,L}. This makes R\mathcal{H}om_X(K,L) a complex with arithmetic Frobenius structure, hence for every integer n it induces a \mathbb{Q}_\ell-linear automorphism F_{\mathrm{coh}} on H^n(X,R\mathcal{H}om_X(K,L)); explicitly, using the standard arithmetic Frobenius structure on the constant sheaf \mathbb{Q}_{\ell,X}, if v:\mathbb{Q}_{\ell,X}\to R\mathcal{H}om_X(K,L)[n] represents a class, then F_{\mathrm{coh}}(v)=\varphi_{\mathcal{H}om}[n]\circ F_Y^*v. For every integer n, there is a canonical \mathbb{Q}_\ell-linear isomorphism \theta_n:\operatorname{Ext}^n_{D^b_c(X,\mathbb{Q}_\ell)}(K,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^n(X,R\mathcal{H}om_X(K,L)). Equip the left-hand side with the arithmetic Frobenius automorphism F_{\mathrm{ext}}(u)=\varphi_L\circ F_Y^*u\circ\varphi_K^{-1} for u:K\to L[n]. Then \theta_n is equivariant for F_{\mathrm{ext}} and F_{\mathrm{coh}}. Equivalently, under \theta_n, the automorphism F_{\mathrm{coh}} corresponds to the automorphism u\mapsto\varphi_L\circ F_Y^*u\circ\varphi_K^{-1} of \operatorname{Ext}^n_{D^b_c(X,\mathbb{Q}_\ell)}(K,L).
lemma_39.proof:
Proof.

Let 1 = Q_ℓ,X. For A,B ∈ D^b_c(X,Q_ℓ), write M_{A,B}=RHom_X(A,B). The internal Hom comes with an evaluation morphism ev_{A,B}:M_{A,B}⊗^L A→B, characterized by the tensor-Hom adjunction Hom(C⊗^L A,B)≅Hom(C,M_{A,B}) for all C. Let λ_A:1⊗^L A→A be the unit isomorphism.

For u:A→B[n], define θ_{A,B}^n(u)∈Hom_D(1,M_{A,B}[n]) as the adjunct of u∘λ_A:1⊗^L A→B[n]. Equivalently, for v:1→M_{A,B}[n], θ_{A,B}^n^{-1}(v)=ev_{A,B}[n]∘(v⊗id_A)∘λ_A^{-1}:A→B[n]. Taking A=K and B=L, and using RΓ(X,M)=RHom_X(1,M), this gives the canonical Q_ℓ-linear isomorphism θ_n:Ext^n_D(K,L)=Hom_D(K,L[n])→Hom_D(1,M_{K,L}[n])=H^n(X,RHom_X(K,L)).

Now define the Frobenius actions. Let F=F_Y and let φ_1:F^*1→1 be the standard arithmetic Frobenius structure on the constant sheaf. For M=M_{K,L} and φ_M=φ_Hom=RHom(φ_K^{-1},φ_L)∘c_{K,L}, set for v:1→M[n]
F_coh(v)=φ_M[n]∘F^*v∘φ_1^{-1}.
These are Q_ℓ-linear automorphisms because F^* is a Q_ℓ-linear autoequivalence and the φ's are isomorphisms. Since φ_1 is the canonical identification F^*1≅1, this is exactly the displayed formula F_coh(v)=φ_Hom[n]∘F^*v in the statement, after the usual identification of F^*1 with 1. For u:K→L[n], set F_ext(u)=φ_L[n]∘F^*u∘φ_K^{-1}.

We need two elementary compatibilities.

(1) Functoriality. If f:A'→A and g:B→B', then for every u:A→B[n],
θ_{A',B'}^n(g[n]∘u∘f)=RHom(f,g)[n]∘θ_{A,B}^n(u).
Proof. Put v=θ_{A,B}^n(u) and w=RHom(f,g)[n]∘v. The defining property of RHom(f,g) with evaluation is
ev_{A',B'}∘(RHom(f,g)⊗id_{A'})=g∘ev_{A,B}∘(id_{M_{A,B}}⊗f).
After shifting by n and applying θ^{-1}, we get
θ_{A',B'}^n^{-1}(w)=ev_{A',B'}[n]∘(RHom(f,g)[n]⊗id_{A'})∘(v⊗id_{A'})∘λ_{A'}^{-1}
=g∘ev_{A,B}[n]∘(id⊗f)∘(v⊗id_{A'})∘λ_{A'}^{-1}.
Naturality of the unit gives f∘λ_{A'}=λ_A∘(id_1⊗f), hence (id⊗f)∘λ_{A'}^{-1}=λ_A^{-1}∘f. Therefore the last expression equals
g∘ev_{A,B}[n]∘(v⊗id_A)∘λ_A^{-1}∘f=g∘θ_{A,B}^n^{-1}(v)∘f=g[n]∘u∘f.
Since θ_{A',B'}^n is bijective, this proves (1).

(2) Compatibility with pullback. For A,B and u:A→B[n], with v=θ_{A,B}^n(u),
θ_{F^*A,F^*B}^n(F^*u)=c_{A,B}[n]∘F^*v∘φ_1^{-1}.
Here c_{A,B}:F^*M_{A,B}→M_{F^*A,F^*B} is defined as the adjunct of F^*ev_{A,B}:F^*(M_{A,B}⊗^L A)→F^*B under the monoidal isomorphism F^*M_{A,B}⊗^L F^*A≅F^*(M_{A,B}⊗^L A). Consequently it satisfies
ev_{F^*A,F^*B}∘(c_{A,B}⊗id_{F^*A})=F^*ev_{A,B}
after the same monoidal identification. Put w=c_{A,B}[n]∘F^*v∘φ_1^{-1}. Then
θ_{F^*A,F^*B}^n^{-1}(w)
=ev_{F^*A,F^*B}[n]∘(c_{A,B}[n]⊗id_{F^*A})∘(F^*v⊗id_{F^*A})∘(φ_1^{-1}⊗id_{F^*A})∘λ_{F^*A}^{-1}.
By monoidality of F^* and compatibility of its unit structure with λ,
(F^*v⊗id_{F^*A})∘(φ_1^{-1}⊗id_{F^*A})∘λ_{F^*A}^{-1}
=F^*((v⊗id_A)∘λ_A^{-1}).
Using the defining compatibility of c_{A,B} with evaluation, the previous displayed expression becomes
F^*ev_{A,B}[n]∘F^*((v⊗id_A)∘λ_A^{-1})
=F^*(ev_{A,B}[n]∘(v⊗id_A)∘λ_A^{-1})
=F^*(θ_{A,B}^n^{-1}(v))=F^*u.
Thus w=θ_{F^*A,F^*B}^n(F^*u), proving (2).

Now take A=K, B=L, M=M_{K,L}, φ_M=φ_Hom, and u∈Ext^n_D(K,L). Let v=θ_n(u). By definition,
F_coh(v)=φ_M[n]∘F^*v∘φ_1^{-1}
=RHom(φ_K^{-1},φ_L)[n]∘c_{K,L}[n]∘F^*v∘φ_1^{-1}.
By (2), c_{K,L}[n]∘F^*v∘φ_1^{-1}=θ_{F^*K,F^*L}^n(F^*u). By (1), applied with f=φ_K^{-1}:K→F^*K and g=φ_L:F^*L→L,
RHom(φ_K^{-1},φ_L)[n]∘θ_{F^*K,F^*L}^n(F^*u)
=θ_{K,L}^n(φ_L[n]∘F^*u∘φ_K^{-1})=θ_n(F_ext(u)).
Therefore θ_n(F_ext(u))=F_coh(θ_n(u)) for every u. This is exactly the required equivariance.

Since θ_n is an isomorphism, the transported automorphism θ_n^{-1}∘F_coh∘θ_n on Ext^n_D(K,L) is precisely u↦φ_L[n]∘F^*u∘φ_K^{-1}. Equivalently, under θ_n, F_coh corresponds to F_ext. This completes the proof.

lemma_44.statement: Let X be a smooth projective variety over F_q, let ell != p, let m >= 1, and let X_m = X x_{Spec F_q} Spec F_{q^m}. For every n >= 0 there is a canonical Q_ell-linear isomorphism H^n_et(X_{overline{F}_q}, Q_ell) = H^n_et((X_m)_{overline{F}_q}, Q_ell) under which arithmetic Frobenius over F_{q^m} corresponds to the m-th power of arithmetic Frobenius over F_q. Consequently arithmetic Frobenius over F_q is semisimple on the left if and only if arithmetic Frobenius over F_{q^m} is semisimple on the right.
lemma_44.proof:
Let Fqbar be the fixed algebraic closure of F_q, and let sigma:Fqbar->Fqbar be sigma(a)=a^q. Let sigma_m:Fqbar->Fqbar be sigma_m(a)=a^{q^m}; then sigma_m=sigma^m. Put Xbar=X x_{F_q} Fqbar and Xmbar=X_m x_{F_{q^m}} Fqbar. Since X_m=X x_{F_q} F_{q^m}, associativity of fiber products gives a canonical isomorphism beta:Xbar->Xmbar. Etale cohomology is functorial, so beta induces the canonical Q_l-linear isomorphism alpha=(beta^{-1})^*:H^n_et(Xbar,Q_l)->H^n_et(Xmbar,Q_l).

The variety X_m is smooth projective over F_{q^m}, because smoothness and projectivity are stable under base change. By lemma_17, Ext^n_{D^b_c(Xbar,Q_l)}(IC_X,IC_X) is finite-dimensional over Q_l; by lemma_3 this Ext group is canonically isomorphic to H^n_et(Xbar,Q_l). Hence V=H^n_et(Xbar,Q_l) is finite-dimensional. Applying the same two lemmas to X_m over F_{q^m} shows V_m=H^n_et(Xmbar,Q_l) is finite-dimensional. By lemma_6a, the arithmetic Frobenius operators on V and V_m are Q_l-linear automorphisms.

Write T=(id_X x sigma)^* on V and S=(id_{X_m} x sigma_m)^* on V_m. Functoriality of pullback gives T^m=(id_X x sigma^m)^*=(id_X x sigma_m)^*. The isomorphism beta is obtained by the identity on X and the identity on the Fqbar factor after the associativity identification; therefore beta composed with (id_X x sigma_m) equals (id_{X_m} x sigma_m) composed with beta. Equivalently, (id_X x sigma_m) composed with beta^{-1} equals beta^{-1} composed with (id_{X_m} x sigma_m). Applying pullbacks and using alpha=(beta^{-1})^* yields S alpha=alpha T^m, where composition of maps is written by juxtaposition. Thus, under alpha, arithmetic Frobenius over F_{q^m} corresponds exactly to the m-th power of arithmetic Frobenius over F_q.

It remains to compare semisimplicity of T and T^m. Since S and T^m are conjugate via the linear isomorphism alpha, lemma_8 implies that S is semisimple if and only if T^m is semisimple. If T is semisimple, then by lemma_5 the operator T tensor_Q_l Q_lbar on V tensor_Q_l Q_lbar is diagonalizable, where Q_lbar is an algebraic closure of Q_l. Its m-th power, which is T^m tensor_Q_l Q_lbar, is also diagonalizable, and lemma_5 applied to T^m gives that T^m is semisimple. Conversely, if T^m is semisimple, then lemma_35(iii), applicable because T is an invertible linear operator by lemma_6a, gives that T is semisimple. Combining these equivalences gives that T is semisimple on V if and only if S is semisimple on V_m, which is the desired consequence.

lemma_48.statement: Let X be a smooth projective variety over F_q of pure dimension d, let k=overline(F_q), and let ell != p be prime. Let F_ar be arithmetic Frobenius on H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell) and F_geo its inverse. If F_ar acts semisimply on H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell[d]) for every n, then F_geo acts semisimply on H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell) for every n, and equivalently on H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell) tensor_{Q_ell} Q_ell_bar.
lemma_48.proof:
Proof. Let k = bar(F_q), and write H^m = H^m_et(X_k,Q_ell) for integers m. The assumption that X has pure dimension d only fixes the shift d; the argument uses the shift isomorphism for any integer d.

First note finiteness. By lemma_17, for every integer i the Q_ell-vector space Ext^i_{D^b_c(X_k,Q_ell)}(IC_X,IC_X) is finite-dimensional, and the induced arithmetic Frobenius map is a Q_ell-linear automorphism. By lemma_3 there is a canonical arithmetic-Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism Ext^i_{D^b_c(X_k,Q_ell)}(IC_X,IC_X) = H^i. Hence each H^i is finite-dimensional and F_ar acts on it as a Q_ell-linear automorphism. Lemma_6a identifies F_geo with F_ar^{-1}.

For every integer n, the shifted constant complex Q_ell[d] satisfies RGamma(X_k,Q_ell[d]) = RGamma(X_k,Q_ell)[d]. Taking cohomology gives a canonical isomorphism s_n: H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell[d]) = H^{n+d}. This isomorphism is F_ar-equivariant. Indeed, arithmetic Frobenius on Q_ell[d] is obtained by applying the same pullback morphism as on Q_ell and then shifting the complex; the functor RGamma commutes with this shift, so the induced maps on cohomology correspond under s_n.

By hypothesis, F_ar is semisimple on H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell[d]) for every integer n. Fix any integer m and put n = m-d. Then s_n is an arithmetic-Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism between finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector spaces. By lemma_8, semisimplicity of F_ar on the source is equivalent to semisimplicity of F_ar on the target. Therefore F_ar is semisimple on H^m.

Since this holds for every m, and F_geo = F_ar^{-1} by lemma_6a, lemma_4 implies that F_geo is semisimple on H^m for every m.

Finally, for each m, apply lemma_5 to the finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector space H^m and the operator F_geo. It states that F_geo is semisimple on H^m if and only if it is semisimple, equivalently diagonalizable, on H^m tensor_{Q_ell} bar(Q_ell). Thus geometric Frobenius acts semisimply on H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell) for every n, and equivalently on H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell) tensor_{Q_ell} bar(Q_ell). QED.

lemma_47.statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let X be a proper variety over F_q, let k=overline(F_q), and let ell != p be prime. Let K be a pure semisimple perverse sheaf on X_k with coefficients in Q_ell_bar and an arithmetic Frobenius isomorphism phi:F_X^*K -> K. Suppose K admits a finite decomposition K ≅ direct sum_alpha direct sum_{j=0}^{d_alpha-1} L_{alpha,j} tensor M_alpha, where each L_{alpha,0} is absolutely simple and pure, L_{alpha,j}=F_X^{j*}L_{alpha,0}, and phi carries L_{alpha,j} tensor M_alpha isomorphically to L_{alpha,j+1} tensor M_alpha with indices taken modulo d_alpha. Suppose that for every alpha the induced automorphism phi^{d_alpha} on the multiplicity space M_alpha is semisimple, and that for every alpha and every n the induced automorphism phi^{d_alpha} on H^n(X_k,L_{alpha,0}) is semisimple. Then phi is semisimple on H^n(X_k,K) for every n.
lemma_47.proof:
Fix n. Write Qbar_l for overline{Q}_l and let Φ be the arithmetic Frobenius automorphism of V^n := H^n(X_k,K) induced by φ. We prove Φ is semisimple.

All vector spaces below are finite-dimensional: each M_α is finite-dimensional by the given finite decomposition, and H^n(X_k,L_{α,0}) is finite-dimensional by the standard finiteness theorem for étale cohomology of constructible sheaves on proper varieties (this is also the finiteness input used in lemma_24).

For each α set K_α = ⊕_{j=0}^{d_α-1} L_{α,j}⊗M_α and V_{α,j}^n = H^n(X_k,L_{α,j})⊗M_α. Since K = ⊕_α K_α is a finite direct sum, and étale cohomology commutes with finite direct sums and with tensoring by a finite-dimensional vector space, there is a canonical decomposition V^n = ⊕_α ⊕_{j=0}^{d_α-1} V_{α,j}^n. The hypothesis on φ says that the induced map Φ carries V_{α,j}^n isomorphically onto V_{α,j+1}^n, with indices taken modulo d_α. This is exactly the Frobenius-orbit decomposition appearing in lemma_24. Applying lemma_24, Φ is semisimple on V^n if and only if for every α the automorphism Φ_α^{d_α} := Φ^{d_α}|_{V_{α,0}^n} is semisimple on V_{α,0}^n. It remains to prove this last assertion.

Fix α and write d=d_α, L_j=L_{α,j}, M=M_α, U_j=H^n(X_k,L_j). Then V_{α,0}^n=U_0⊗M. Let T_j: U_j⊗M → U_{j+1}⊗M be the transition map induced by φ (indices modulo d), so that Φ|_{V_{α,j}^n}=T_j. We identify T_j as a tensor product. Frobenius pullback gives an isomorphism f_j: U_j → U_{j+1}. The sheaf part of φ after this pullback is an endomorphism of L_{j+1}⊗M. Since L_{α,0} is absolutely simple and F_X^* is an autoequivalence, each L_j is absolutely simple, so End(L_{j+1})=Qbar_l. Choosing a basis of M identifies L_{j+1}⊗M with a finite direct sum of copies of L_{j+1}; hence an endomorphism of L_{j+1}⊗M is uniquely of the form id_{L_{j+1}}⊗b_j for some b_j∈GL(M). Consequently T_j=f_j⊗b_j.

Composing the T_j for j=0,...,d-1 gives Φ^{d}|_{U_0⊗M} = (f_{d-1}∘...∘f_0) ⊗ (b_{d-1}∘...∘b_0). The first factor is exactly the induced automorphism φ^{d} on H^n(X_k,L_{α,0}) mentioned in the hypotheses; call it A_{α,n}. The second factor is exactly the induced automorphism φ^{d} on the multiplicity space M_α; call it B_α. Thus Φ_α^{d_α}=A_{α,n}⊗B_α.

By hypothesis A_{α,n} and B_α are semisimple. Since Qbar_l is algebraically closed and U_0 and M are finite-dimensional, choose bases of U_0 and M consisting of eigenvectors for A_{α,n} and B_α respectively. If A_{α,n}u=λu and B_αm=μm, then (A_{α,n}⊗B_α)(u⊗m)=λμ(u⊗m). The tensor products of the two eigenbases form a basis of U_0⊗M consisting of eigenvectors. Hence A_{α,n}⊗B_α is semisimple. This is the linear-algebra conclusion of lemma_35(i), applied over Qbar_l.

Therefore Φ_α^{d_α} is semisimple on V_{α,0}^n for every α. By lemma_24, Φ is semisimple on V^n. Since n was arbitrary, φ is semisimple on H^n(X_k,K) for every n.

lemma_52.statement: Let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety over F_q of pure dimension d, let k=overline(F_q), and let l != p. For every integer n there is a canonical arithmetic-Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism of Q_l-vector spaces H^n(X_k,Q_l[d]) -> H^{n+d}(X_k,Q_l), where the left side denotes hypercohomology of the shifted constant sheaf. Consequently arithmetic Frobenius is semisimple on H^n(X_k,Q_l[d]) for all n if and only if it is semisimple on H^m(X_k,Q_l) for all m.
lemma_52.proof:
Let k=overline(F_q) and let F=F_ar:X_k->X_k be the q-power arithmetic Frobenius. Here H^n(X_k,-) denotes hypercohomology, i.e. the cohomology of RGamma(X_k,-). We use the cohomological shift convention (K[d])^n=K^{n+d}. For any bounded constructible complex K on X_k, choose a functorial K-injective resolution I(K). Since I(K)[d] is a K-injective resolution of K[d] and Gamma(X_k,I(K)[d])=Gamma(X_k,I(K))[d], the derived global-sections functor satisfies a canonical isomorphism RGamma(X_k,K[d])=RGamma(X_k,K)[d] in D(Q_l). Taking cohomology gives canonical isomorphisms psi_n(K):H^n(X_k,K[d])->H^{n+d}(X_k,K). These isomorphisms are natural in K: if u:K->L is a morphism, then psi_n(L) composed with the map induced by u[d] equals the map induced by u composed with psi_n(K). Applying this to the constant sheaf Q_l placed in degree 0 gives canonical isomorphisms psi_n:H^n(X_k,Q_l[d])->H^{n+d}(X_k,Q_l).

First note that the vector spaces involved are finite-dimensional and the Frobenius operators are invertible. Since X is smooth projective, lemma_3 gives, for every m>=0, a Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism Ext^m_{D^b_c(X_k,Q_l)}(IC_X,IC_X) ≅ H^m_et(X_k,Q_l). By lemma_17, Ext^m_{D^b_c(X_k,Q_l)}(IC_X,IC_X) is finite-dimensional over Q_l and the induced arithmetic Frobenius map is a Q_l-linear automorphism. Hence H^m_et(X_k,Q_l) is finite-dimensional and arithmetic Frobenius is invertible on it for m>=0; for m<0 it is the zero space. Through psi_n, the same finiteness and invertibility hold for H^n(X_k,Q_l[d]).

It remains to prove equivariance. The constant sheaf Q_l has its canonical arithmetic Frobenius structure phi:F^*Q_l->Q_l. The induced structure on the shifted complex is phi[d]:F^*(Q_l[d])=(F^*Q_l)[d]->Q_l[d]. Let T'_n be the operator on H^n(X_k,Q_l[d]) induced by the composite RGamma(X_k,Q_l[d]) -> RGamma(X_k,F^*(Q_l[d])) -> RGamma(X_k,Q_l[d]), the first map being pullback along F and the second being RGamma(phi[d]). Let T_{n+d} be the analogous composite for Q_l. Pullback commutes with shift: F^*(Q_l[d])=(F^*Q_l)[d], and under the canonical identification RGamma(X_k,F^*(Q_l[d]))=RGamma(X_k,F^*Q_l)[d] the map induced by pullback for Q_l[d] is the d-shift of the map induced by pullback for Q_l. Likewise the map induced by phi[d] is the d-shift of the map induced by phi. Therefore the endomorphism of RGamma(X_k,Q_l[d]) defining T'_n is the d-shift of the endomorphism of RGamma(X_k,Q_l) defining T_{n+d}. By naturality of psi with respect to shifted endomorphisms, psi_n T'_n = T_{n+d} psi_n. Thus psi_n is arithmetic-Frobenius-equivariant.

For each fixed n, psi_n is an isomorphism of finite-dimensional Q_l-vector spaces intertwining the two invertible arithmetic Frobenius operators. By lemma_8, T'_n is semisimple if and only if T_{n+d} is semisimple. The assignment m=n+d is a bijection from the integers to the integers. Consequently, T'_n is semisimple for every integer n if and only if T_m is semisimple for every integer m. The zero vector spaces occurring in negative degrees carry the identity automorphism, which is semisimple, so the equivalence is unaffected by those degrees. This proves the lemma.

lemma_53.statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let X be a proper variety over F_q, let k=overline(F_q), and let ell != p be prime. Let L be an absolutely simple perverse sheaf on X_k with coefficients in Q_ell_bar, and let d >= 1 be minimal such that F_X^{d*}L is isomorphic to L, where F_X is the q-power arithmetic Frobenius on X_k. For any two isomorphisms phi, psi: F_X^{d*}L -> L and any integer n, the induced Q_ell_bar-linear automorphisms F_phi and F_psi of H^n(X_k,L) differ by multiplication by a nonzero scalar in Q_ell_bar^*. In particular, F_phi is semisimple on H^n(X_k,L) if and only if F_psi is semisimple on H^n(X_k,L).
lemma_53.proof:
Let F = F_X and F_d = F^d. Since F is the q-power arithmetic Frobenius on X_k, it is an automorphism of the scheme X_k; its inverse is the automorphism induced by the inverse field automorphism of k. Hence F_d is also an automorphism of X_k. Pullback by F_d is therefore a Q_l_bar-linear autoequivalence of D^b_c(X_k,Q_l_bar), and for every object M it induces a Q_l_bar-linear isomorphism (F_d)^*: H^n(X_k,M) -> H^n(X_k,F_d^*M). For an isomorphism alpha: F_d^*L -> L, define the induced automorphism F_alpha of H^n(X_k,L) by F_alpha = H^n(alpha) o (F_d)^*.

We first prove that End_{D^b_c(X_k,Q_l_bar)}(L) = Q_l_bar. Choose one of the given isomorphisms, say phi, and let Y = X x_{F_q} Spec F_{q^d}. Then Y is proper over F_{q^d}, its geometric fiber is Y_k = X_k, and the q^d-power arithmetic Frobenius on Y_k is F_d. The isomorphism phi: F_d^*L -> L is therefore an arithmetic Frobenius structure on L over F_{q^d}. Since L is absolutely simple, it is a simple perverse sheaf, hence a finite direct sum of simple perverse sheaves. Applying lemma_20 to Y and K = L shows that Ext^0_{D^b_c(X_k,Q_l_bar)}(L,L) is finite-dimensional over Q_l_bar. The perverse sheaves form the heart of the perverse t-structure, and for objects A,B in the heart the natural map Hom_heart(A,B) -> Hom_D(A,B) is an isomorphism in degree zero. Therefore End_D(L) = End_Perv(L). Since L is simple, Schur's lemma gives that End_Perv(L) is a division algebra over Q_l_bar. A finite-dimensional division algebra over an algebraically closed field is the field itself: for any element a of the division algebra, the commutative subalgebra Q_l_bar[a] is a finite-dimensional domain over Q_l_bar, hence a field, hence equals Q_l_bar; thus a lies in Q_l_bar. Consequently End_D(L) = Q_l_bar.

Now let phi, psi: F_d^*L -> L be any two isomorphisms. The composite psi o phi^{-1} is an automorphism of L in the derived category, hence an element of End_D(L). By the previous paragraph there is a scalar c in Q_l_bar with psi o phi^{-1} = c id_L. Since psi o phi^{-1} is an isomorphism, c is nonzero. Thus psi = c phi. Applying the cohomology functor gives H^n(psi) = c H^n(phi), and therefore F_psi = H^n(psi) o (F_d)^* = c H^n(phi) o (F_d)^* = c F_phi. This proves that the two induced automorphisms differ by multiplication by a nonzero scalar.

Finally, let V = H^n(X_k,L) and T = F_phi. If V = 0, semisimplicity is trivial. Otherwise, T and cT have exactly the same invariant subspaces: a subspace W is T-stable if and only if T(W) is contained in W, which is equivalent to cT(W) being contained in W because c is nonzero. Thus T is semisimple if and only if cT is semisimple. Equivalently, over the algebraically closed field Q_l_bar, if T is diagonalizable then cT has the same eigenvectors with eigenvalues multiplied by c, and the converse is obtained by replacing c with c^{-1}. Applying this to T = F_phi and cT = F_psi gives that F_phi is semisimple on H^n(X_k,L) if and only if F_psi is semisimple on H^n(X_k,L).

lemma_45_finite_frob.statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let X be a proper variety over F_q, let k=overline(F_q), and let ell != p be prime. Let K be an object of D^b_c(X_k,Q_ell) equipped with an arithmetic Frobenius isomorphism phi: F_X^* K -> K, where F_X is the q-power arithmetic Frobenius morphism on X_k. Equip the constant sheaf Q_ell on X_k with its natural arithmetic Frobenius isomorphism psi: F_X^* Q_ell -> Q_ell. Then for every integer n, the hypercohomology H^n(X_k,K) is finite-dimensional over Q_ell. Moreover, the canonical isomorphism H^n(X_k,K) isomorphic to Ext^n_{D^b_c(X_k,Q_ell)}(Q_ell,K) transports to H^n(X_k,K) a canonical Q_ell-linear arithmetic Frobenius automorphism F_phi induced by phi; under the Ext identification this automorphism is u maps to phi o F_X^*(u) o psi^{-1}.
lemma_45_finite_frob.proof:
Proof. Let k=\overline{\mathbb F}_q and let D=D^b_c(X_k,\mathbb Q_\ell). Write Q=\mathbb Q_{\ell,X_k} for the constant sheaf on X_k, and let F_X:X_k\to X_k be the q-power arithmetic Frobenius automorphism. Since k is algebraically closed, F_X is an automorphism, so F_X^* is a \mathbb Q_\ell-linear autoequivalence of D.

The sheaf Q is an object of D: it is locally constant on X_k, hence constructible. It is equipped with its natural arithmetic Frobenius isomorphism \psi:F_X^*Q\xrightarrow{\sim}Q. By hypothesis K is an object of D equipped with \varphi:F_X^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}K.

1. Finite-dimensionality of the relevant Ext groups. Apply lemma_16_frob_stable to the pair of objects Q and K, with their Frobenius structures \psi and \varphi. It gives, for every integer n, that Ext^n_D(Q,K) is finite-dimensional over \mathbb Q_\ell.

2. Canonical identification with hypercohomology. Lemma_39, applied to the first object Q and the second object K, gives a canonical \mathbb Q_\ell-linear isomorphism
\theta_n: Ext^n_D(Q,K) \xrightarrow{\sim} H^n(X_k,R\mathcal{H}om_X(Q,K)).
There is also a canonical isomorphism in D
\eta_K: R\mathcal{H}om_X(Q,K) \xrightarrow{\sim} K.
Indeed, for a sheaf F of \mathbb Q_\ell-vector spaces, \mathcal{H}om(Q,F)\cong F by sending a local morphism f:Q|_U\to F|_U to f(1_U), where 1_U is the local section of Q corresponding to 1\in\mathbb Q_\ell; since Q is the unit (locally free of rank one), this isomorphism is exact and hence holds in the derived category. Taking hypercohomology gives an isomorphism
\eta_{n}: H^n(X_k,R\mathcal{H}om_X(Q,K)) \xrightarrow{\sim} H^n(X_k,K).
Define
\beta_n = \eta_{n}\circ\theta_n: Ext^n_D(Q,K) \xrightarrow{\sim} H^n(X_k,K).
Equivalently, \beta_n^{-1} is the canonical isomorphism H^n(X_k,K)\cong Ext^n_D(Q,K) coming from the derived identification R\Gamma(X_k,K)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_{X_k}(Q,K).

Since Ext^n_D(Q,K) is finite-dimensional and \beta_n is an isomorphism, H^n(X_k,K) is finite-dimensional over \mathbb Q_\ell.

3. The Frobenius automorphism on Ext. For u\in Ext^n_D(Q,K)=\operatorname{Hom}_D(Q,K[n]), define
T_n(u)=\varphi\circ F_X^*(u)\circ\psi^{-1},
where \varphi and \psi are implicitly shifted to degree n. Here F_X^*(u):F_X^*Q\to F_X^*K[n], \psi^{-1}:Q\to F_X^*Q, and \varphi:F_X^*K\to K, so T_n(u) is again a morphism Q\to K[n]. The operation is \mathbb Q_\ell-linear because pullback by F_X and composition with \mathbb Q_\ell-linear isomorphisms are \mathbb Q_\ell-linear. It is bijective: its inverse is
T_n^{-1}(v)=(F_X^*)^{-1}(\varphi^{-1}\circ v\circ\psi)
for v\in\operatorname{Hom}_D(Q,K[n]), where (F_X^*)^{-1}=F_X^{-1*} is the pullback along the inverse automorphism of F_X. Indeed,
T_n(T_n^{-1}(v))=\varphi\circ F_X^*((F_X^*)^{-1}(\varphi^{-1}\circ v\circ\psi))\circ\psi^{-1}=\varphi\circ\varphi^{-1}\circ v\circ\psi\circ\psi^{-1}=v,
and similarly T_n^{-1}(T_n(u))=u.

By lemma_39, this automorphism T_n is exactly the arithmetic Frobenius automorphism induced on Ext^n_D(Q,K) by the Frobenius structures \psi on Q and \varphi on K: the statement of lemma_39 says that under the equivariant isomorphism \theta_n the induced automorphism corresponds to u\mapsto\varphi\circ F_X^*(u)\circ\psi^{-1}.

4. Transport to hypercohomology. The unit isomorphism \eta_K is compatible with the Frobenius structures. Explicitly, if \varphi_{\mathcal{H}om}=R\mathcal{H}om(\psi^{-1},\varphi)\circ c_{Q,K} is the induced Frobenius on R\mathcal{H}om(Q,K), then
\eta_K\circ\varphi_{\mathcal{H}om}=\varphi\circ F_X^*\eta_K.
This is the formal compatibility of the unit isomorphism R\mathcal{H}om(Q,-)\cong \operatorname{Id} with pullback and the given Frobenius structures; on the level of sheaves it says that a morphism f:Q\to K is determined by f(1), and the induced Frobenius sends f(1) to \varphi(F_X^*(f(1))). Hence \eta_K is arithmetic-Frobenius-equivariant, and the same holds after taking hypercohomology. Consequently \beta_n intertwines T_n with the canonical arithmetic Frobenius automorphism on H^n(X_k,K) induced by \varphi.

Define F_\varphi on H^n(X_k,K) by
F_\varphi=\beta_n\circ T_n\circ\beta_n^{-1}.
Then F_\varphi is a \mathbb Q_\ell-linear automorphism of the finite-dimensional vector space H^n(X_k,K). By the previous paragraph it is the canonical arithmetic Frobenius automorphism induced by \varphi. Finally, under the canonical identification \beta_n^{-1}:H^n(X_k,K)\cong Ext^n_D(Q,K), the automorphism F_\varphi is transported to T_n; explicitly, for u\in Ext^n_D(Q,K),
\beta_n^{-1}(F_\varphi(\beta_n(u)))=T_n(u)=\varphi\circ F_X^*(u)\circ\psi^{-1}.
This completes the proof.

lemma_49.statement: Let f:Y -> X be a finite surjective morphism of smooth projective geometrically connected varieties over F_q, let k=overline(F_q), and let ell != p be prime. If arithmetic Frobenius acts semisimply on H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell) for every n, then arithmetic Frobenius acts semisimply on H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell) for every n.
lemma_49.proof:
Fix an integer n >= 0 and write
  V_X := H^n_et(X_k, Q_ell),   V_Y := H^n_et(Y_k, Q_ell),
and denote by F_X : V_X -> V_X and F_Y : V_Y -> V_Y the q-power arithmetic Frobenius operators.

Step 1 (finite-dimensionality; F is invertible). Both X and Y are proper over F_q (they are projective). The constant sheaf Q_{ell,X} on X_k, equipped with its standard arithmetic Frobenius isomorphism psi : F_X^* Q_{ell,X} -> Q_{ell,X}, is an object of D^b_c(X_k, Q_ell) with Frobenius structure, so lemma_45_finite_frob applied with K = Q_{ell,X} gives that H^n(X_k, Q_{ell,X}) = V_X is finite-dimensional over Q_ell; the same argument with Y in place of X shows V_Y is finite-dimensional. By lemma_6a, the pullback by the q-power field automorphism gives Q_ell-linear automorphisms F_ar of each H^n(-_k, Q_ell) (with inverse the geometric Frobenius); thus F_X and F_Y are invertible Q_ell-linear operators on finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector spaces.

Step 2 (the pullback realises V_X as a Frobenius-stable direct summand of V_Y). The morphism f : Y -> X satisfies the hypotheses of lemma_36 (finite surjective of smooth projective geometrically connected varieties over F_q). Hence, with d = deg f >= 1,
  (i) f^* : V_X -> V_Y is injective,
  (ii) f^* is equivariant for arithmetic Frobenius: F_Y o f^* = f^* o F_X,
  (iii) f_* o f^* = d id_{V_X}, so (1/d) f_* : V_Y -> V_X is a linear retraction of f^* (d is a nonzero integer, hence invertible in Q_ell).
Put W := f^*(V_X) subset V_Y. Then:
  (a) W is F_Y-stable: for w = f^*(x) in W one has F_Y(w) = F_Y f^*(x) = f^*(F_X x) in W, by (ii).
  (b) W is a direct summand of V_Y as a Q_ell-vector space: concretely, r := f^* o (1/d) f_* : V_Y -> V_Y is an idempotent (using (iii): r^2 = f^* (1/d f_* f^*) (1/d) f_* = f^* (1/d f_*) = r) whose image is W, so V_Y = W oplus ker(r); equivalently, any basis of W extends to a basis of V_Y.
  (c) f^* : V_X -> W is a Q_ell-linear isomorphism (injective by (i), surjective onto W by definition), and by (ii) it intertwines F_X with the restricted operator F_Y|_W : W -> W.

Step 3 (semisimplicity restricts to a stable direct summand). By hypothesis F_Y acts semisimply on V_Y. Since W is an F_Y-stable direct summand of V_Y (Step 2(a),(b)), lemma_35(ii) applied to T = F_Y, V = V_Y, U = W gives that F_Y|_W is semisimple on W. For completeness we recall the direct linear-algebra reason this is the right conclusion: because char(Q_ell) = 0, semisimplicity of F_Y on V_Y is equivalent to its minimal polynomial m(t) in Q_ell[t] being a product of distinct irreducible factors. The polynomial m(F_Y|_W) is the restriction of m(F_Y) = 0 to the invariant subspace W, hence m(F_Y|_W) = 0, so the minimal polynomial m_W(t) of F_Y|_W divides m(t) and is therefore again a product of distinct irreducibles; by the same criterion F_Y|_W is semisimple. (Equivalently, over Q_ell_bar the operator F_Y is diagonalisable with eigenspace decomposition V_Y oplus ... = (+)_lambda E_lambda, the spectral projections P_lambda = product_{mu != lambda} (F_Y - mu)/(lambda - mu) are polynomials in F_Y and hence preserve W, giving W = (+)_lambda (W cap E_lambda), so F_Y|_W is diagonalisable.)

Step 4 (descent along the Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism). Apply lemma_8 with V = V_X and T_V = F_X, with W' = W and T_{W'} = F_Y|_W, and with alpha = f^* : V_X -> W, which is a Q_ell-linear isomorphism satisfying alpha o T_V = T_{W'} o alpha by Step 2(c). Lemma_8 then yields: F_X is semisimple on V_X if and only if F_Y|_W is semisimple on W. By Step 3 the latter holds, so F_X acts semisimply on V_X = H^n_et(X_k, Q_ell).

Step 5 (conclusion and edge cases). The integer n >= 0 was arbitrary, so arithmetic Frobenius acts semisimply on H^n_et(X_k, Q_ell) for every n >= 0. If for some n one has V_X = 0 (for instance n > 2 dim X), then W = 0 and the conclusion is vacuous; the argument above covers this case verbatim, since the identity operator on the zero space is semisimple. Note also that only the injectivity and Frobenius-equivariance of f^* were used, so no hypothesis on the degree d relative to ell is needed; and the geometric connectedness of X and Y is used exactly to supply the hypotheses of lemma_36. This proves the lemma.

lemma_55.statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let X be a proper variety over F_q, let k=overline(F_q), and let ell != p. Let L be an absolutely simple perverse sheaf on X_k with coefficients in Q_l_bar. Suppose that for some integer d >= 1 there is an isomorphism phi:F_X^{d*}L -> L, where F_X is the q-power arithmetic Frobenius automorphism of X_k. Let e >= 1 be the minimal integer for which F_X^{e*}L is isomorphic to L, and let psi:F_X^{e*}L -> L be any such isomorphism. For an isomorphism alpha:F_X^{r*}L -> L, define T_alpha to be the automorphism of H^n(X_k,L) obtained by first applying the pullback isomorphism H^n(X_k,L) -> H^n(X_k,F_X^{r*}L) induced by F_X^{r*} and then applying alpha_*. Then e divides d. If m=d/e, there exists a nonzero scalar c in Q_l_bar such that, for every n, T_phi = c * (T_psi)^m on H^n(X_k,L). Consequently T_phi is semisimple if and only if T_psi is semisimple. In particular, to prove semisimplicity for all such pairs (d,phi), it is enough to prove it in the minimal-period case d=e for one, equivalently every, choice of psi.
lemma_55.proof:
We fix the following notation. Write $F:=F_X$ for the $q$-power arithmetic Frobenius automorphism of $X_k$, $\mathcal D:=D^b_c(X_k,\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell)$ for the derived category, and $\mathrm{Perv}\subset\mathcal D$ for the abelian category of perverse sheaves (the heart of the perverse $t$-structure). For $r\ge 0$, $F^{r*}$ is the $r$-fold pullback; it is an auto-equivalence of $\mathcal D$, because $F$ is an automorphism of the scheme $X_k$ (indeed a universal homeomorphism, so pullback on the small \'etale topos is an exact equivalence). All cohomology groups $H^n(X_k,-)$ below are hypercohomology with $\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$-coefficients, and $u_*$ denotes the map on hypercohomology induced by a morphism $u$ of $\mathcal D$.

**Step 0: the pullback maps and their formal properties.** For $r\ge 0$ put $F_r:=F^r:X_k\to X_k$. The adjunction unit $\eta_M:M\to R{F_r}_*F_r^*M$ together with the canonical functorial isomorphism $R\Gamma(X_k,R{F_r}_*(-))\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(X_k,-)$ (coming from $\Gamma(X_k,{F_r}_*A)=A({F_r}^{-1}X_k)=A(X_k)$) defines a $\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$-linear map
$$\Phi_r=\Phi_r(M):H^n(X_k,M)\longrightarrow H^n(X_k,F^{r*}M).$$
These maps satisfy:
(P1) $\Phi_0=\mathrm{id}$ and $\Phi_s\circ\Phi_r=\Phi_{r+s}$, using $F^{s*}F^{r*}=(F_r\circ F_s)^*=F^{(r+s)*}$;
(P2) each $\Phi_r$ is an isomorphism, with inverse $\Phi_{-r}:=\Phi_r(F_r^{-1})$ defined by pullback along the inverse automorphism $F^{-r}$; indeed $\Phi_r\circ\Phi_{-r}=\Phi_0=\mathrm{id}$ and conversely by (P1);
(P3) (naturality) for every $u:M\to N$ in $\mathcal D$ one has $\Phi_r\circ u_*=(F^{r*}u)_*\circ\Phi_r$, because $\eta$ is a natural transformation and the identification $R\Gamma(X_k,R{F_r}_*(-))\cong R\Gamma(X_k,-)$ is functorial;
(P4) $u\mapsto u_*$ is $\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$-linear on Hom spaces and respects composition: $(v\circ u)_*=v_*\circ u_*$, $(\lambda u+\mu v)_*=\lambda u_*+\mu v_*$, $(\mathrm{id})_*=\mathrm{id}$; this is just additivity of the functor $R\Gamma(X_k,-)$ on the triangulated category of complexes of $\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$-sheaves.

For an isomorphism $\alpha:F^{r*}L\xrightarrow{\sim}L$ the operator of the statement is $T_\alpha:=\alpha_*\circ\Phi_r$, an automorphism of $H^n(X_k,L)$ by (P2).

**Step 1: $e$ divides $d$.** Consider the stabiliser
$$\mathrm{Stab}:=\{\,r\in\mathbb Z:\; F^{r*}L\simeq L \text{ in }\mathcal D\,\}.$$
It is a subgroup of $\mathbb Z$: $0\in\mathrm{Stab}$ trivially; if $r,s\in\mathrm{Stab}$ then $F^{(r+s)*}L=F^{r*}(F^{s*}L)\simeq F^{r*}L\simeq L$ (pullback by a fixed functor sends isomorphic objects to isomorphic objects), so $r+s\in\mathrm{Stab}$; and if $r\in\mathrm{Stab}$, applying the equivalence $F^{-r*}$ to an isomorphism $F^{r*}L\simeq L$ gives $L\simeq F^{-r*}L$, so $-r\in\mathrm{Stab}$. (For completeness: $\mathrm{Stab}\neq\{0\}$ because a constructible complex on $X_k$ is defined over $X_{\mathbb F_{q^N}}$ for some $N\ge1$ — standard limit/descent argument — and then $F^{N*}L\simeq L$, since for the projection $\mathrm{pr}:X_k\to X_{\mathbb F_{q^N}}$ one has $\mathrm{pr}\circ F^N=\mathrm{pr}$ and $L\simeq\mathrm{pr}^*L_0$.) By hypothesis $d\in\mathrm{Stab}$, and $e$ is the minimal positive element of $\mathrm{Stab}$. Since $\mathrm{Stab}$ is a non-zero subgroup of $\mathbb Z$, $\mathrm{Stab}=e_0\mathbb Z$ where $e_0\ge1$ is its least positive element; by minimality of $e$ we get $e_0=e$, hence $\mathrm{Stab}=e\mathbb Z$ and $e\mid d$. Write $m:=d/e\;(\ge1)$.

**Step 2: the $m$-fold composite structure and the power of $T_\psi$.** For $j=1,\dots,m$ set $\psi_j:=F^{(j-1)e*}(\psi):F^{je*}L\xrightarrow{\sim}F^{(j-1)e*}L$ (an isomorphism, being the image of $\psi$ under the functor $F^{(j-1)e*}$), and define
$$\Psi:=\psi_1\circ\psi_2\circ\cdots\circ\psi_m:\;F^{me*}L=F^{d*}L\xrightarrow{\sim}L.$$
Claim: $(T_\psi)^m=T_\Psi$ on $H^n(X_k,L)$, for every $n$. We argue by induction on $m$. For $m=1$ there is nothing to prove. Suppose the claim holds for $m$, with $\Psi_m:=\psi_1\circ\cdots\circ\psi_m:F^{me*}L\to L$. Then, using (P3) with $u=\Psi_m:M=F^{me*}L\to N=L$, and then (P1) and (P4):
$$ (T_\psi)^{m+1}=T_\psi\circ T_{\Psi_m}=(\psi_*\circ\Phi_e)\circ((\Psi_m)_*\circ\Phi_{me})=\psi_*\circ\big(\Phi_e\circ(\Psi_m)_*\big)\circ\Phi_{me}=\psi_*\circ\big((F^{e*}\Psi_m)_*\circ\Phi_e\big)\circ\Phi_{me}=(\psi\circ F^{e*}\Psi_m)_*\circ\Phi_{(m+1)e}=T_{\Psi_{m+1}},$$
and $\psi\circ F^{e*}\Psi_m=\psi_1\circ(\psi_2\circ\cdots\circ\psi_{m+1})=\Psi_{m+1}$, since $F^{e*}\psi_j=\psi_{j+1}$ and $F^{e*}F^{(j-1)e*}=F^{je*}$. This completes the induction; the case $m=2$ reads explicitly $T_\psi^2=\psi_*\Phi_e\psi_*\Phi_e=\psi_*(F^{e*}\psi)_*\Phi_{2e}=T_{\psi\circ F^{e*}\psi}$, as a check.

**Step 3: $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(F^{d*}L,L)$ is one-dimensional, so $\varphi=c\,\Psi$.** Composition with the isomorphism $\Psi$ gives a $\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$-linear isomorphism $\mathrm{End}_{\mathcal D}(L)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(F^{d*}L,L)$, $g\mapsto g\circ\Psi$. Since $L$ lies in the heart $\mathrm{Perv}$ and the inclusion of the heart of a $t$-structure is fully faithful, $\mathrm{End}_{\mathcal D}(L)=\mathrm{End}_{\mathrm{Perv}}(L)$. Because $L$ is absolutely simple, Schur's lemma gives that $\mathrm{End}_{\mathrm{Perv}}(L)$ is a division algebra and absolute simplicity means precisely $\mathrm{End}_{\mathrm{Perv}}(L)=\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell\cdot\mathrm{id}_L$ (for reference: this is automatic once $\mathrm{End}_{\mathrm{Perv}}(L)$ is known to be finite-dimensional over $\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$, since $\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$ is algebraically closed and a finite-dimensional division algebra over an algebraically closed field is the field itself). Hence $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(F^{d*}L,L)=\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell\cdot\Psi$ is one-dimensional. The given $\varphi:F^{d*}L\xrightarrow{\sim}L$ is an element of this space, so $\varphi=c\,\Psi$ for a unique $c\in\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$; as both $\varphi$ and $\Psi$ are isomorphisms, $c\ne0$. Note that $c$ is determined in $\mathcal D$, hence is independent of $n$.

**Step 4: the relation between the operators.** Using (P4) and Step 2,
$$T_\varphi=\varphi_*\circ\Phi_d=(c\,\Psi)_*\circ\Phi_d=c\,(\Psi_*\circ\Phi_d)=c\,T_\Psi=c\,(T_\psi)^m\qquad\text{on }H^n(X_k,L),$$
for every $n$, with the same non-zero scalar $c$.

**Step 5: linear algebra.** Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $\Omega$ of characteristic $0$, $T\in\mathrm{GL}(V)$, $m\ge1$, $c\in\Omega^*$; write $V_\chi:=\ker(T-\chi)$ and, for $\lambda$, $W_\lambda:=\ker(T^m-\lambda)$.
(a) $T$ is semisimple $\iff$ $cT$ is semisimple. Indeed the eigenspace of $cT$ for the eigenvalue $\lambda$ is $\ker(cT-\lambda)=\ker(T-\lambda/c)=V_{\lambda/c}$, so $V$ is a direct sum of eigenspaces of $T$ if and only if it is one for $cT$.
(b) $T$ is semisimple $\iff$ $T^m$ is semisimple.
"$\Leftarrow$": assume $V=\bigoplus_{\lambda}W_\lambda$ (direct sum of eigenspaces of $T^m$). Since $T$ is invertible, every eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $T^m$ is non-zero. $T$ preserves each $W_\lambda$ because $T$ commutes with $T^m$. For $w\in W_\lambda$ consider $U:=\mathrm{span}_\Omega\{w,Tw,\dots,T^{m-1}w\}$; it is $T$-stable, since $T(T^{m-1}w)=T^mw=\lambda w\in U$. The polynomial $X^m-\lambda$ annihilates $T|_U$; its derivative $mX^{m-1}$ has only the root $0$, which is not a root of $X^m-\lambda$ as $\lambda\ne0$, so $X^m-\lambda$ has $m$ distinct roots, and being $\Omega=\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$ algebraically closed it splits into distinct linear factors. Hence $U$ is a direct sum of eigenspaces of $T|_U$, and in particular $w$ is a sum of eigenvectors of $T$. Thus $V$ is spanned by eigenvectors of $T$; sums of eigenspaces for distinct eigenvalues are direct (eigenvectors belonging to distinct eigenvalues are linearly independent, by the standard induction on the number of eigenvalues), so $V=\bigoplus_\chi V_\chi$, i.e. $T$ is semisimple.
"$\Rightarrow$": assume $V=\bigoplus_\chi V_\chi$. Group the summands as $W_\lambda:=\bigoplus_{\chi:\,\chi^m=\lambda}V_\chi$; $T^m$ acts as $\lambda$ on $W_\lambda$. If $T^mv=\lambda v$ with $v=\sum_\chi v_\chi$ a finite sum, then $\sum_\chi(\chi^m-\lambda)v_\chi=0$ and directness forces $v_\chi=0$ unless $\chi^m=\lambda$; hence $W_\lambda=\ker(T^m-\lambda)$ and $V=\bigoplus_\lambda W_\lambda$, i.e. $T^m$ is semisimple.

Apply Step 5 with $\Omega=\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$, $V=H^n(X_k,L)$, $T=T_\psi$ (invertible, as $\psi$ is an isomorphism and $\Phi_e$ is one by (P2)), $c$ and $m$ as in Step 4. By (a) and the relation $T_\varphi=c(T_\psi)^m$, $T_\varphi$ is semisimple if and only if $(T_\psi)^m$ is semisimple; by (b) this holds if and only if $T_\psi$ is semisimple. This proves the asserted equivalence, for every $n$.

**Step 6: the reduction to the minimal-period case.** Assume semisimplicity is known in the case $d=e$ for one isomorphism $\psi_0:F^{e*}L\xrightarrow{\sim}L$. Let $d\ge1$ and $\varphi:F^{d*}L\xrightarrow{\sim}L$ be arbitrary. Step 1 gives $e\mid d$ with $m=d/e$, and Steps 2–4 applied with $\psi=\psi_0$ give $T_\varphi=c\,(T_{\psi_0})^m$ with $c\ne0$. Since $T_{\psi_0}$ is semisimple, Step 5(b) ("$\Rightarrow$") makes $(T_{\psi_0})^m$ semisimple, and Step 5(a) then makes $c\,(T_{\psi_0})^m=T_\varphi$ semisimple. The converse direction is immediate because the case $d=e$ is among the pairs $(d,\varphi)$. Finally, in the minimal-period case the choice of $\psi$ is immaterial: this is exactly lemma_53 (with $e$ minimal, any two isomorphisms $\psi,\psi':F^{e*}L\to L$ induce automorphisms of $H^n(X_k,L)$ differing by a non-zero scalar, so semisimplicity for one implies it for the other); equivalently it is the special case $m=1$ of the relation $T_\varphi=c\,T_\psi$ proved above. Hence it suffices to prove semisimplicity in the minimal-period case $d=e$ for one, equivalently every, choice of $\psi$.

All claims are established: $e\mid d$; with $m=d/e$ there is $c\in\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell^*$, independent of $n$, with $T_\varphi=c\,(T_\psi)^m$ on $H^n(X_k,L)$; $T_\varphi$ is semisimple if and only if $T_\psi$ is; and the stated reduction holds.

lemma_56.statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety over F_q of pure dimension d, let k=overline{F}_q, and let l != p be prime. The natural scalar-extension map End_{Perv(X_k,Q_l)}(Q_l[d]) tensor_{Q_l} Q_l_bar -> End_{Perv(X_k,Q_l_bar)}(Q_l_bar[d]) is an isomorphism of Q_l_bar-algebras; both endomorphism algebras are canonically isomorphic to the base field; and the canonical arithmetic Frobenius structure on Q_l_bar[d] induces the identity automorphism on End_{Perv(X_k,Q_l_bar)}(Q_l_bar[d]).
lemma_56.proof:
Write k = \overline{\mathbb F}_q, \Lambda = \mathbb Q_\ell, \bar\Lambda = \overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell, X_k = X\times_{\mathbb F_q}k, D = D^b_c(X_k,\Lambda), \bar D = D^b_c(X_k,\bar\Lambda). Since X is geometrically connected over \mathbb F_q, X_k is connected; since X is smooth of pure dimension d over \mathbb F_q, X_k is smooth of pure dimension d over the algebraically closed field k.

STEP 1 (both objects are perverse; endomorphisms in the heart = Hom in the derived category). By lemma_11, \Lambda[d] is a perverse sheaf on X_k. The extension-of-scalars functor -\otimes_\Lambda \bar\Lambda : Sh(X_k,\Lambda)\to Sh(X_k,\bar\Lambda) is exact because \bar\Lambda is a flat \Lambda-module, and exactness implies it commutes with the sheaf-cohomology functors {}^iH. The perverse t-structure on D^b_c is defined by amplitude conditions on the {}^iH (the support/cosupport conditions), so -\otimes_\Lambda\bar\Lambda preserves the t-structure and is t-exact; it restricts to an exact functor Perv(X_k,\Lambda)\to Perv(X_k,\bar\Lambda). As \Lambda[d]\otimes_\Lambda\bar\Lambda = \bar\Lambda[d] (extension of scalars of the constant sheaf is the constant sheaf with extended value), \bar\Lambda[d]\in Perv(X_k,\bar\Lambda). For objects of the heart of a t-structure, Hom in the heart equals Hom in the derived category, hence
  End_{Perv(X_k,\Lambda)}(\Lambda[d]) = Hom_D(\Lambda[d],\Lambda[d]),   End_{Perv(X_k,\bar\Lambda)}(\bar\Lambda[d]) = Hom_{\bar D}(\bar\Lambda[d],\bar\Lambda[d]).

STEP 2 (reducing Hom to H^0 of the constant sheaf, as algebras). For A = \Lambda or \bar\Lambda and K,L\in D^b_c(X_k,A) the internal-Hom adjunction against the unit object A gives a canonical isomorphism
  Hom(K,L) \;\xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}\; Hom(A,\,R\mathcal Hom(K,L)) \;\xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}\; H^0(X_k, R\mathcal Hom(K,L)),
natural in K and L, which identifies the composition pairing on the left with the one on the right induced by the multiplication morphism R\mathcal Hom(K,L)\otimes^L R\mathcal Hom(L,M)\to R\mathcal Hom(K,M).

Take K=L=\Lambda[d]. By lemma_14 (X is smooth projective of pure dimension d) there is a canonical arithmetic-Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism in D^b_c(X_k,\Lambda)
  R\mathcal Hom(\Lambda[d],\Lambda[d]) \cong \Lambda .
This canonical isomorphism is an isomorphism of algebra objects. Indeed it is the unit map \Lambda\to R\mathcal Hom(\Lambda[d],\Lambda[d]), 1\mapsto \mathrm{id}; since \Lambda[d] is the shift of the monoidal unit, R\mathcal Hom(\Lambda[d],\Lambda[d]) \cong \Lambda[d]^\vee\otimes^L\Lambda[d] with \Lambda[d]^\vee = R\mathcal Hom(\Lambda[d],\Lambda)=\Lambda[-d], so \Lambda[d]^\vee\otimes^L\Lambda[d]\cong\Lambda, and under this identification the composition pairing is the canonical pairing \Lambda\otimes\Lambda\to\Lambda. Equivalently, one checks the statement on the small étale site of a strictly henselian local scheme, where \Lambda[d] is the free rank-one complex concentrated in one degree, and the claim becomes the elementary chain-level fact that the degree-zero endomorphism ring of a free rank-one complex is the ground ring with composition = multiplication. Combining with the adjunction of Step 2 gives a canonical isomorphism of \Lambda-algebras
  \theta_\Lambda:\ End_{Perv(X_k,\Lambda)}(\Lambda[d]) \xrightarrow{\sim} H^0(X_k,\Lambda),  \quad \theta_\Lambda^{-1}(\lambda)=\lambda\cdot\mathrm{id}.

The same holds with \bar\Lambda coefficients. Since \Lambda[d] is a perfect complex (locally quasi-isomorphic to a finite free \Lambda-module in one degree), the base-change morphism
  R\mathcal Hom(\Lambda[d],\Lambda[d])\otimes^L_\Lambda \bar\Lambda \longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom(\Lambda[d]\otimes^L\bar\Lambda,\ \Lambda[d]\otimes^L\bar\Lambda)=R\mathcal Hom(\bar\Lambda[d],\bar\Lambda[d])
is an isomorphism in \bar D (standard property of internal Hom out of a perfect object; locally it is Hom_\Lambda(\Lambda,\Lambda)\otimes\bar\Lambda=Hom_{\bar\Lambda}(\bar\Lambda,\bar\Lambda)), isomorphism of algebra objects. Transporting the algebra structure of lemma_14 along it yields a canonical isomorphism of algebra objects R\mathcal Hom(\bar\Lambda[d],\bar\Lambda[d])\cong\bar\Lambda, hence a canonical isomorphism of \bar\Lambda-algebras
  \theta_{\bar\Lambda}:\ End_{Perv(X_k,\bar\Lambda)}(\bar\Lambda[d]) \xrightarrow{\sim} H^0(X_k,\bar\Lambda), \quad \theta_{\bar\Lambda}^{-1}(\lambda)=\lambda\cdot\mathrm{id}.

STEP 3 (H^0). For each n\ge 1 the constant sheaf \mathbb Z/\ell^n on X_{k,\text{ét}} is represented by the étale X_k-scheme \coprod_{\mathbb Z/\ell^n}X_k; hence \Gamma(X_k,\mathbb Z/\ell^n)=\mathrm{Hom}_{X_k}(X_k,\coprod X_k) is the set of open-and-closed decompositions of X_k indexed by \mathbb Z/\ell^n.
